questions.title: Who will score India's first half-century in the July 2026 Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe?
questions.background: A half-century in cricket is an individual score of at least 50 runs in one innings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the first Indian batter to reach 50 runs in an innings during the July 2026 men's Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe, according to official match scorecards and contemporaneous match reports. Resolution Date : 2026-07-23 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the batter's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 7-14 batting form and lineup update ahead of the July 23 Zimbabwe T20I series (Hindustan Times July 12-14, Khaleej Times July 12-13): BCCI's July 12 squad revision replaced only injured bowler Varun Chakaravarthy with Ravi Bishnoi, leaving the Zimbabwe batting squad intact. However, India lost 0-4 to England and 0-2 to Ireland, and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi failed in all three England T20Is (42 runs across 3 innings, never crossing 20) before being DROPPED for the 5th T20I in Southampton. July 13-14 reporting notes 'it remains to be seen whether he gets any game time' in Zimbabwe, with maiden call-up right-handed opener Prabhsimran Singh (or promoted WK opener Ishan Kishan) creating ~50-55% risk that Sooryavanshi is benched for the 1st T20I in Harare (when India's first 50 is most likely scored). Cutting Sooryavanshi sharply 0.17 -> 0.11 (#4), elevating captain Shreyas Iyer 0.13 -> 0.16 (#3, cited by HT July 12 as the only Indian batter who looked accomplished in England and guaranteed #3/#4 starter), boosting locked-in opener Abhishek Sharma 0.26 -> 0.28 (prior Harare T20I centurion) and guaranteed top-3 starter Ishan Kishan 0.21 -> 0.23 (world #1 T20I batter, could also open), and holding vice-captain Tilak Varma at 0.10 (guaranteed #4/#5 starter with improved 5th T20I form), leaving 12% residual led by Prabhsimran Singh (~8%), Shivam Dube (~2%), and Rinku Singh (~1.5%).

questions.title: Which European country will declare a national emergency in response to wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements or reliable news reporting published by July 25, 2026. Resolution Condition : Identify the European country whose national government declares a national emergency because of wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026. Regional or local emergency declarations alone do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-19 escalation in Spain (AFP/Straits Times July 19): the wildfire north of Madrid in Guadalajara (Castilla-La Mancha / Sierra Norte Natural Park) exploded six-fold in 48 hours from ~2,000 ha on July 17 to over 12,000 ha on July 19, forcing hundreds of evacuations, while the Zaragoza/Aragon blaze simultaneously grew to nearly 16,000 ha and remained 'far from under control' as of the evening of July 18—giving Spain ~28,000 ha actively burning across two autonomous communities right after July's 13-death Almeria fire and as AEMET's 42-44C heatwave peaks. Because simultaneous multi-region mega-fires directly trigger Spain's statutory criteria for a central-government Nivel 3 Emergencia de Interes Nacional (or Council of Ministers emergency declaration on Tuesday July 21), Spain jumps (+0.08, 0.26 -> 0.34) into #1. With no European national wildfire emergency yet declared through July 19 and only 6 days left in the July 1-25 window, Portugal trims (0.27 -> 0.24, still strong #2 under its active mainland State of Alert and the same Iberian heatwave), Greece trims (0.14 -> 0.12), North Macedonia trims (0.11 -> 0.10), and Italy (0.03, frequent Council of Ministers Stato di Emergenza user under July Mediterranean heat) replaces France (0.03 -> residual tail after Fontainebleau containment and cooler thunderstorms), leaving 17% tail mass for Bulgaria, Cyprus, Albania, Croatia, Montenegro, Turkey, and France.

questions.background: The Commonwealth Games men's team gymnastics competition awards medals according to the final team standings.

questions.current_reasoning: Two major developments since June 24 significantly narrow the England-Canada gap ahead of the July 24 Glasgow 2026 men's team final: (1) Three-time Olympic champion Max Whitlock withdrew on July 13 with a hand injury sustained in training (BBC Sport, Reuters), removing an elite pommel horse specialist and disrupting England's late-stage lineup, while Team England's Chef de Mission noted the squad mixes Olympic/world medallists with several multi-sport debutants; (2) Gymnastics Canada officially named a powerhouse A-team on July 3—Paris Olympians Félix Dolci, René Cournoyer, and William Émard plus Jordan Carroll and Ethan Ikeda—fresh off winning historic team gold at the 2026 Pan American Championships (with Émard winning rings gold and Carroll pommel horse silver). England remains the clear favorite given its unmatched all-around/apparatus depth and three straight CWG team titles, but trims 0.74 -> 0.64 while Canada jumps sharply 0.13 -> 0.25; Australia (young squad, 4 debutants) trims 0.06 -> 0.05, Cyprus holds 0.03, and host Scotland trims 0.03 -> 0.02 (1% residual).

questions.title: What type of munition will be confirmed destroyed in Syria's first OPCW-verified chemical-weapons destruction operation since 2014?
questions.background: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) verifies the destruction of chemical weapons and associated munitions.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the type of munition identified as destroyed in Syria's first OPCW-verified chemical-munitions destruction operation since 2014, as reported to the UN Security Council by 2026-09-03. Resolution Date : 2026-09-03 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the specific munition type, excluding its quantity.
questions.current_reasoning: Major OPCW development on 2026-07-09: at its 112th session, the OPCW Executive Council reinstated Syria's voting rights and formally approved a detailed verification plan for the destruction of Category 3 chemical weapons at Al Qutayfah (37 km north of Damascus), alongside facility agreements for the Al Qutayfah and Homs CW storage sites (OPCW press release, AP News July 9). Under the CWC, Category 3 strictly denotes unfilled military chemical munitions and devices—effectively excluding improvised industrial chlorine cylinders (0.06 -> removed) from this first operation and concentrating probability on the two unfilled Assad-era binary munition types highlighted in OPCW's May 27 discovery report: aerial bombs of the Ltamenah/Khan Shaykhun type (0.38 -> 0.42) and rockets of the Ghouta type (0.32 -> 0.34). Artillery shells hold at 0.07, unfilled missile warheads enter at 0.05 reflecting Al Qutayfah's historical missile/CW depot role and Syria's prior Category 3 inventory, mortar shells edge to 0.04, and 8% tail mass covers other specific Category 3 designations or devices.

questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official club or player announcement, or reliable contemporaneous sports reporting confirming a completed move. questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-19 transfer collapse for Colo-Colo (TVN.cl, Cooperativa.cl, RedGol.cl citing Cesar Luis Merlo and Fabrizio Romano): Colo-Colo has moved on from Vozinha and reached an agreement to sign Uruguayan international goalkeeper Santiago Mele from Monterrey on a one-year loan with purchase option. Romano reported Vozinha's talks with Colo-Colo were 'on the verge of collapse' after a new round of negotiations, and Merlo declared 'Santiago Mele is Colo-Colo's new reinforcement... Vozinha never went past an offer,' while RedGol notes the 40-year-old free agent is now evaluating other unnamed offers (mostly from South America per Romano). Cutting Colo-Colo sharply from 0.40 -> 0.02 (retaining only tiny deal-collapse/medical risk). Because ge.globo confirmed Brazilian clubs Ceara, Avai, and Atletico Goianiense declined to open talks (and Corinthians rejected him), and no new specific South American bidder has yet been named, we place 85% probability mass in the unnamed residual while keeping modest calibrated placeholders on previously linked clubs: Inter Miami (0.09, highest-profile July link despite carrying three GKs), Colo-Colo (0.02), Cruz Azul (0.02, earlier Liga MX link), Ceara (0.01), and Avai (0.01).

local_articles.snippet: If anything has kept NBA fans on edge during this free agency, it's none other than LeBron James' decision on his next destination. local_articles.title: LeBron James' photo-matched Miami Heat jersey from record-setting 2014 game heads to auction with $50,000 estimate
local_articles.snippet: A game-worn Miami Heat jersey worn by LeBron James during a historic milestone in his career is heading to auction, with bidding expected to top $50,000. The black Miami Heat away jersey was worn by James on April 12, 2014, during Miami's final regular-season game of the 2013-14 season. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Miami Heat 98-85, but James finished the game with a record 27 points, eight rebounds and five assists. The performance marked James' 10th consecutive NBA season averaging at least 25 points, five rebounds and five assists, breaking a record previously held by Hall of Famer Oscar Robertson, who accomplished the feat nine times. James has since extended that streak to 20 consecutive seasons, a mark no other player in NBA history has matched. questions.title: Which circuit will Formula One announce as the replacement venue for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix?
questions.background: The Bahrain Grand Prix originally scheduled for April 2026 was cancelled amid conflict in the Middle East.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Formula One's first official announcement after May 1, 2026 identifying a replacement host circuit for the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix. Resolution Conditions : The announcement must occur by December 31, 2026. Resolution is based on the announced venue, regardless of whether the race is subsequently held or receives final regulatory approval. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the circuit.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-18 major refresh (first since June 24, incorporating Crash.net July 5 and F1Oversteer/Nextgen Auto July 15): F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali stated on July 5 that F1 aims to fill the vacant Oct 4 slot (between Baku and Singapore) with a decision required before the summer break following the July 26 Hungarian GP. With Middle East conflict continuing (July 17 IRGC al-Tanf strike claim and ongoing Strait of Hormuz closure) clouding any return to the Gulf, F1 chiefs are evaluating European/regional replacements. New July 15 reporting significantly reshuffles candidate odds: (1) Istanbul Park formally offered to step in ahead of its 2027 deal and fits the Baku-to-Singapore Oct 4 geography best, but faces rushed renovation/homologation hurdles and lower crowd projections, trimming it from 0.40 -> 0.30; (2) Algarve International Circuit (Portimao) was explicitly highlighted in both July 5 Crash.net and July 15 F1Oversteer reports as ready to step in ahead of its 2027 deal with a valid Grade 1 licence, lifting it sharply from 0.15 -> 0.23; (3) Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari (Imola) remains a prime turnkey Grade 1 option named July 15 (0.21 -> 0.19); (4) Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya enters at 0.10 after circuit chiefs formally offered a second 2026 race and July 15 reporting named Barcelona alongside Imola and Portimao as the most likely option if teams block FOM's preferred double-header; (5) Baku City Circuit enters at 0.04 (replacing unmentioned Sepang/Paul Ricard) as FOM's preferred double-header option adjacent to Oct 4 despite current team opposition. Top-5 sum = 0.86, leaving 0.14 for Sepang, Mugello, Paul Ricard, Singapore/Las Vegas double-headers, or other Grade 1 tracks.

Weighting Tier-1 BBC Sport/AFP/L'Equipe reporting (PSG personal-terms edge, active Leipzig talks alongside Akliouche, Ramos and Lee Kang-in sold) alongside Sport Bild's multi-club update cuts Paris Saint-Germain sharply (0.55 -> 0.38), lifts Liverpool (0.24 -> 0.28), brings Manchester City (0.12) and Manchester United (0.09) into the top 5 (pushing Chelsea and Real Madrid into the 9% residual tail), and keeps Bayern Munich at 0.04 (explicitly named earlier by RB chief Mintzlaff).

local_articles.title: Chelsea sign forward Malard from Manchester United
local_articles.snippet: July 20 - Chelsea have signed forward Melvine Malard from Manchester United on a four-year contract, the Women's Super League club said on Monday. • The 26-year-old France international joins Chelsea after three seasons at Manchester United and will be reunited with manager Sonia Bompastor, who coached her at Olympique Lyonnais and guided the club to the Women's Champions League title in 2022. • Malard joined United in 2023 and went on to register 21 goal contributions in 57 appearances across her tenure. She also helped the club lift the Women's FA Cup in her debut season. • A regular in the France squad, Malard has earned 41 caps and scored 14 international goals, representing her country at both Euro 2022 and Euro 2025. • "My objective is to become better every single day and to win trophies. local_articles.title: 'Legendary' former Liverpool and England star Keegan dies aged 75
local_articles.snippet: Former Liverpool and England star Kevin Keegan has died aged 75 after battling cancer, his family announced on Monday. Keegan, regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation, was diagnosed with stage four cancer and underwent treatment in January. "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75," a statement from Keegan's family said. "The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments." Keegan, a dynamic striker nicknamed "mighty mouse", won the English top-flight title three times with Liverpool after starting his legendary career with lowly Scunthorpe. He also won the European Cup in 1977 and the FA Cup in 1974 during an iconic six-year spell at Anfield before joining German club Hamburg in 1977. local_articles.snippet: Kevin Keegan, the former England and Newcastle manager who was twice European football of the year and a stalwart member of Liverpool’s serial First Division and European champions in the 1970s, has died aged 75.
